articles.title: Emergency contact and reunification plan
articles.summary: Create a plan that works when family members are separated and phones fail.
body: List every household member and their usual locations during the day.
Choose two meeting places: one immediately outside the home and one outside the neighborhood.
Choose an out of area contact who can relay short status messages.
Write each person’s phone numbers, relevant accessibility needs, and pickup permissions on a paper card.
Agree on who retrieves children, who checks on dependent adults, and how to report a change of plan.
Practice the plan, including an exercise without mobile data.
Store copies in bags, vehicles, and a protected household folder.
Safety note: Do not publish sensitive personal details in the shared library.

articles.title: Household hazard walk through
articles.summary: Identify preventable household hazards before a disruption.
body: Walk each room and identify blocked exits, unsecured heavy furniture, damaged cords, and overloaded outlets.
Check that smoke and carbon monoxide alarms are installed and working according to manufacturer instructions.
Locate water, gas, and electrical shutoff controls and document who is qualified to operate them.
Inspect exterior drainage, trees, loose objects, and access routes without entering unsafe areas.
Prioritize hazards by potential severity and ease of correction.
Record actions, responsible person, and completion date.
Repeat after major repairs, storms, or household changes.
Safety note: Never touch damaged electrical equipment or investigate suspected gas leaks. Leave the area and contact appropriate responders.

articles.title: Emergency kit inspection cycle
articles.summary: Maintain emergency supplies through recurring inspection.
body: Create an inventory listing item, quantity, location, expiration date, and condition.
Separate essential daily medications and items that require special handling from general supplies.
Check flashlights, radio batteries, chargers, and cables using their normal operating procedures.
Inspect sealed food and water for damaged containers and follow manufacturer storage instructions.
Replace expired or damaged items and record the replacement date.
Check clothing and footwear sizes for children.
Set a recurring calendar reminder and repeat after using the kit.
Safety note: Follow medication storage guidance; do not substitute expired or damaged medicines based on this checklist.

articles.title: Safe flashlight and battery use
articles.summary: Use portable lighting while reducing fire and battery hazards.
body: Prefer purpose built LED flashlights or lanterns over open flames.
Check device and battery labels for compatible chemistry, size, and charging requirements.
Inspect for swelling, leakage, corrosion, heat, or damage before use.
Keep spare batteries protected against short circuits and away from heat and moisture.
Use manufacturer approved charging equipment and a stable, ventilated charging surface.
Assign lights to fixed locations and verify each light works during periodic inspections.
Recycle damaged batteries through an appropriate collection program.
Safety note: Do not charge swollen or damaged batteries; avoid mixing incompatible battery types.

articles.title: Refrigerator and freezer outage log
articles.summary: Track temperature and time during a power interruption.
body: Record the time power was lost and the last known safe appliance temperatures.
Keep refrigerator and freezer doors closed as much as practical.
Use appliance thermometers to measure actual temperatures when available.
Record each opening, observed temperature, and time on a paper log.
Consult current USDA or local public health guidance before deciding which perishable foods to retain.
Discard food when safety is uncertain; smell and appearance cannot establish safety.
Clean and dry the appliance after spoiled food is removed.
Safety note: Food safety thresholds depend on measured temperature and elapsed time; verify current USDA guidance.

articles.title: Paper communications message form
articles.summary: Record accurate messages for handoff when networks are unreliable.
body: Start a log with date, local time, time zone, station or sender identifier, and operator name.
For each message record recipient, sender, priority, exact text, and the time received.
Read back critical names, numbers, locations, and instructions to confirm accuracy.
Mark messages as pending, delivered, or unable to deliver, including the time and method.
Use plain language and avoid transmitting sensitive personal information unnecessarily.
Preserve original entries; correct mistakes with an annotated update rather than silently erasing.
Transfer completed logs to the designated records custodian.
Safety note: Transmit only on frequencies and services for which you are authorized; do not treat unverified reports as confirmed.

articles.title: Household water storage inventory
articles.summary: Track stored water without assuming unknown water is potable.
body: List each container, its volume, fill date, source, and storage location.
Use containers intended for drinking water and follow their cleaning instructions.
Keep containers sealed and protected from heat, sunlight, fuel, and chemicals.
Inspect for damage, leaks, unusual odor, or contamination before use.
Record household water needs, including pets and medical or accessibility requirements.
Maintain a separate label for water that is not verified safe for drinking.
Follow current local health authority instructions during boil water or do not drink advisories.
Safety note: Boiling does not remove chemical contamination; follow the specific advisory and use an alternative safe supply when instructed.
articles.source_review: Pending article specific source verification and qualified editorial review.

articles.title: Shelter room selection checklist
articles.summary: Identify safer interior refuge options for different hazards.
body: Identify the specific hazard before selecting a room; flood, tornado, smoke, and extreme heat require different actions.
Consult local emergency management guidance for designated shelters and evacuation orders.
For tornado risk, identify a small interior room on the lowest suitable level, away from windows, when no rated safe room is available.
For flood risk, avoid basements and low areas and follow evacuation instructions.
Verify exits, communication options, accessibility, and space for all household members.
Stage a flashlight, shoes, communications device, and essential supplies.
Practice reaching the selected area without relying on electricity.
Safety note: A single room is not safe for every hazard; do not shelter in a flood prone basement.

articles.title: Storm debris documentation
articles.summary: Document property damage without entering unsafe areas.
body: Wait until officials indicate it is safe to access the property.
Photograph visible damage from safe positions before cleanup where practical.
Record date, location, approximate dimensions, and affected property for each item.
Keep receipts for emergency repairs, lodging, and necessary supplies.
Separate debris by local collection rules without touching downed lines or unknown chemicals.
Use appropriate protective equipment for permitted cleanup tasks.
Back up photos and notes locally and keep a paper summary for insurance or assistance applications.
Safety note: Avoid unstable structures, floodwater, exposed wiring, and suspicious containers; request professional assistance.

articles.title: Evacuation departure checklist
articles.summary: Use a repeatable process to leave promptly when instructed.
body: Check official evacuation instructions and the latest route restrictions.
Account for household members and confirm the destination and alternate destination.
Pack essential medicines, identification, accessibility equipment, pet supplies, and communications devices.
Notify the designated contact of departure and intended route without sharing sensitive details publicly.
Secure the home only if doing so does not delay a required evacuation.
Record departure time, vehicle fuel level, and planned check in points.
Avoid flooded roads and obey road closure instructions.
Safety note: Do not delay evacuation to complete a checklist or retrieve property.

articles.title: Generator placement and carbon monoxide precautions
articles.summary: Reduce lethal exhaust and electrical hazards from portable generators.
body: Read the generator manual and identify its exhaust outlet before operation.
Operate portable fuel powered generators outdoors only, well away from doors, windows, vents, and occupied structures.
Never operate a generator in a garage, basement, enclosed porch, or near an opening, even with doors open.
Use working carbon monoxide alarms inside occupied buildings.
Keep the generator dry and follow manufacturer instructions for cords and connected loads.
Never connect a generator to household wiring without properly installed transfer equipment by a qualified electrician.
Shut down and allow cooling before refueling according to the manufacturer.
Safety note: Carbon monoxide is odorless and can kill quickly. If an alarm sounds or symptoms develop, move everyone to fresh air and seek emergency help.

articles.title: Smoke alarm response and exit drill
articles.summary: Practice rapid exit when a smoke alarm activates.
body: Identify two ways out of each sleeping area where possible.
Keep exit paths clear and agree on an outdoor meeting point.
Test alarms according to the manufacturer and local requirements.
Practice exiting low under smoke during drills without creating smoke or fire.
If an alarm sounds, leave immediately and close doors behind you when safe.
Once outside, call emergency services and report anyone missing.
Never reenter a burning building.
Safety note: Do not spend time collecting belongings or attempt to investigate a growing fire.

articles.title: Extreme heat household check plan
articles.summary: Coordinate safe check ins during dangerous heat.
body: Monitor official heat alerts and local cooling center announcements.
Identify people who may need extra help, including older adults, young children, and those without reliable cooling.
Agree on check in times and backup communication methods.
Identify a safe, accessible cooled location and a transport plan.
Keep drinking water available and follow individual medical advice about fluid restrictions.
Recognize confusion, fainting, and other signs of severe heat illness as reasons for urgent medical help.
Document missed check ins and activate the agreed escalation plan.
Safety note: Heat stroke is a medical emergency. Call emergency services for altered mental status or other severe symptoms.

articles.title: Emergency sanitation station setup
articles.summary: Organize hand hygiene and waste handling when normal plumbing is interrupted.
body: Determine whether public health or utility officials have issued sewage or water restrictions.
Separate handwashing, food preparation, and waste handling areas.
Provide soap and a safe water source for handwashing when available.
Use lined, closable waste containers and keep them away from food and children.
Follow local public health instructions for toilet alternatives and waste disposal.
Wear suitable gloves for handling waste and wash hands afterward.
Inspect the station regularly and replenish supplies.
Safety note: Do not discharge waste into floodwater, waterways, or storm drains; local rules govern disposal.

articles.title: Medication and medical equipment continuity list
articles.summary: Document essential health supplies for an evacuation or outage.
body: Create a private list of prescribed medicines, dose instructions from the label, prescriber, and pharmacy contact.
List equipment that depends on electricity, refrigeration, consumables, or routine servicing.
Ask the treating clinician or pharmacist about safe backup arrangements and travel storage.
Identify charging and backup power needs from device manuals.
Keep essential documentation accessible to authorized caregivers.
Review the list after medication or equipment changes.
Protect records from unauthorized access and keep an offline copy.
Safety note: Do not change medication doses or use improvised power connections based on this list.

articles.title: Neighborhood welfare check coordination
articles.summary: Organize voluntary checks without creating additional risk.
body: Confirm whether local emergency management has issued movement restrictions.
Create a voluntary roster with only necessary contact and accessibility information.
Assign pairs to safe, authorized areas and establish check in times.
Use a standard status form: contact made, assistance requested, unable to contact, and referral.
Escalate medical emergencies to professional responders rather than attempting unsupported interventions.
Keep personal information confidential and limit sharing to authorized helpers.
Record completed checks and outstanding requests.
Safety note: Never enter damaged buildings, floodwater, or restricted areas to complete a welfare check.

articles.title: Portable radio readiness inspection
articles.summary: Confirm handheld radio readiness before deployment.
body: Verify radio model, charged battery, spare power, antenna, and approved accessories.
Check that programmed channels match the applicable communications plan.
Confirm time, location, callsign or identifier, and legal operating authority.
Perform a brief radio check on an appropriate channel without unnecessary traffic.
Record receive and transmit performance, battery condition, and faults.
Pack a paper frequency and contact plan as permitted by the organization.
Keep radios dry and protect connectors during transport.
Safety note: Never transmit on public safety or other restricted channels without authorization.

articles.title: Paper map and route backup
articles.summary: Preserve basic navigation when GPS or data service fails.
body: Obtain a current paper map covering home, destination, and alternate routes.
Mark major roads, bridges, known flood areas, shelters, and meeting points.
Write addresses and phone numbers for destinations on a separate card.
Practice orienting the map using visible landmarks.
Check official road closures before travel when information is available.
Keep maps in a protective sleeve and a spare copy in the vehicle.
Revisit routes after construction, seasonal flooding, or other changes.
Safety note: Never cross barricades or drive through floodwater based on a paper route plan.
articles.source_review: Pending article specific source verification and qualified editorial review.

articles.title: Portable power bank rotation
articles.summary: Keep backup charging equipment serviceable.
body: List power banks by capacity, supported ports, and assigned device.
Inspect cases, cables, and connectors for damage or swelling.
Charge and store according to the manufacturer’s temperature and state of charge guidance.
Test charging with each essential device and note compatible cables.
Label each bank with its last inspection date.
Rotate units so one remains ready for immediate use.
Dispose of damaged lithium batteries through appropriate collection channels.
Safety note: Do not use, puncture, or charge swollen, leaking, or overheating batteries.
articles.source_review: Pending article specific source verification and qualified editorial review.

articles.title: Document backup and offline access
articles.summary: Preserve important reference files during a connectivity outage.
body: Identify documents needed for immediate decisions, including contacts, plans, maps, and manuals.
Store a working copy on a device that can open files without internet access.
Create a second copy on separate removable storage or another trusted device.
Encrypt sensitive records where appropriate and keep recovery information secure.
Test opening the files while the device is disconnected from all networks.
Record backup date, storage location, and responsible custodian.
Refresh copies when important information changes.
Safety note: A file being visible in a cloud app does not guarantee offline availability; test actual access.
